saints.name: St. Henry
saints.title: Holy Roman Emperor
saints.shortBlurb: An emperor who governed his realm as a servant of the Church and the poor…
biography: Born in 973, son of Duke Henry the Quarrelsome of Bavaria, Henry spent his youth partly in exile, formed by Bishop Wolfgang of Regensburg and at the cathedral school of Hildesheim. Duke of Bavaria from 995, he won the German crown on the death of Otto III in 1002, was crowned king of Italy in 1004, and received the imperial crown from Benedict VIII at Rome on 14 February 1014.

His reign was consumed by three wars with Bolesław of Poland, yet he governed as a servant of the Church: he restored the see of Merseburg for the Slav missions, promoted monastic reform and clerical discipline, and in 1007 founded the diocese of Bamberg, endowing it so richly that its cathedral became his monument and, in the end, his tomb.

His marriage to Cunegund, herself later canonized, was childless, and legend tells that he begged admission to a monastery only to be charged by the abbot to keep ruling as his obedience. He died near Göttingen on 13 July 1024 and was canonized by Eugene III in 1146, the only German king among the saints. He is patron of the childless, of dukes, and of those rejected by religious orders.
saints.knownFor: Governing the empire in the service of the Church and founding Bamberg.
